source: The plays: this app's plain-word labels for the offer types in $100M Money Models. Each opens when the numbers say it applies, the way a moon opens on the Planets page. The steps are checklists to run the play; the 'when' rules are plain conditions over recipes and facts, evaluated in moneymodels/engines/model.js.
confidenceNote: The opening conditions are this app's reading of when each play tends to pay off, not the book's figures.
note: when: a list of { of, op, value } where `of` is a recipe or fact id, op is one of >=, <=, >, <, ==, known. Every rule must hold for the play to open. Until then the play says what it is waiting on.

plays.label: Win your money back
plays.what: The customer pays, and gets it back (or as credit) if they hit a stated result and follow the rules. Most will not; the ones who do are the customers you want.

when.says: gross margin of at least 50%, so a refund does not sink you
a promise with a result you can measure

steps: Write the result and the deadline as a number anyone can check
List every rule they must follow to qualify (attendance, submissions, check-ins)
Decide: cash refund, or credit toward the upsell
Put the refund cost in the attraction offer's delivery cost
Track who qualifies, and offer them the upsell first

plays.label: Giveaway
plays.what: One big prize, many entrants, and everyone who did not win gets an offer. Cheap leads at volume.

when.says: a cost per lead of $20 or more, so cheaper leads matter

steps: Pick a prize worth a lot to the customer and a known cost to you
Set the entry: a form, a follow, a referral
Write the consolation offer every non-winner gets
Set a draw date and announce it
Count entrants, buyers of the consolation offer, and cost

plays.label: Decoy
plays.what: A free or very cheap option next to the real one, so the real one looks like the sensible choice and the free one filters out people who would never pay.

when.says: a paid attraction offer for the decoy to sit beside

steps: Design the decoy: less of the real thing, clearly worse value per dollar
Show both side by side, the decoy first
Make the decoy's string lead to the paid offer
Count who picks which
Raise the decoy's price if too many take it

plays.label: Buy some, get some free
plays.what: Bundle volume up front. The free part is margin you would have spent on getting the customer back anyway.

when.says: gross margin of at least 60%, so the free units cost you little

steps: Pick the unit (sessions, months, boxes)
Set the bundle so the free part is under a third of the total
Price the bundle above the single unit times the paid count
Say the free part out loud in the offer
Compare cash per customer with the single-unit offer

plays.label: Pay less now or pay more later
plays.what: Two prices for the same thing: a smaller one paid today and a larger one paid on results or over time. Both close; one brings cash forward.

when.says: a main offer of $500 or more, where the two prices differ enough to matter

steps: Set the pay-now price
Set the pay-later price 20 to 40% higher
Decide the later trigger: a date, a result, an instalment
Present both, pay-now first
Track which is chosen and the cash collected inside 30 days

plays.label: Free with strings
plays.what: Free only when the string (a deposit, a booked call, an upsell moment) makes the free customer pay off.

when.says: an upsell with a known profit per customer
the cost of a customer

steps: Name the string: what they must do to get the free thing
Put the upsell inside the string (the results call, the fitting, the pickup)
Take a refundable deposit if no-shows are likely
Count free takers, string completers, and upsell takers
Kill it if free customers do not reach the upsell

plays.label: Classic upsell
plays.what: The next thing they need to get the result faster or keep it.

when.says: an attraction offer with a price and a cost

steps: Name the next obstacle after the attraction offer
Build the thing that removes it
Price it above the attraction offer
Write the one-sentence ask
Ask every customer, and tally it

plays.label: Menu upsell
plays.what: Several add-ons, they pick. People say yes to something more often than to one thing.

when.says: an upsell take rate under 30%, where choice tends to help

steps: List three to five add-ons that each move the result
Price each so any two beat the single upsell
Present the menu after the first yes
Count which combinations sell
Drop the one nobody picks

plays.label: Anchor upsell
plays.what: Show the biggest option first. The one you want to sell looks reasonable next to it.

when.says: an upsell of $1,000 or more, where the anchor has room above it

steps: Design the top tier as if someone will buy it
Price it at least three times the real upsell
Present it first, then the real one
Count anchor buyers separately
Raise the real upsell's price if the take rate holds

plays.label: Rollover upsell
plays.what: Credit what they just paid toward the bigger thing. The first purchase becomes a deposit.

when.says: a paid attraction offer to roll over
an upsell price

steps: State the credit: 'the [attraction price] you paid comes off'
Set a deadline on the credit (this week, this visit)
Show the upsell price after the credit
Track rollover takers against ordinary takers
Widen the credit if the take rate is low

plays.label: Payment plan
plays.what: The same offer split over time. Usually the first thing to try.

when.says: an upsell of $300 or more, where splitting helps

steps: Set the number of payments (three is common)
Make the first payment the largest
Put every plan on automatic billing
Offer it only after the no, never on the price list
Track plans to their last payment

plays.label: Trial with a string
plays.what: Try it, and pay if you keep it, or pay a penalty if you do not do the work.

when.says: a continuity offer for the trial to lead into

steps: Set the trial length (shorter than the first win)
Write the string: the payment or penalty, and its trigger
Take card details up front
Check in before the trial ends
Count trial starts, conversions and penalties

plays.label: Lighter version
plays.what: Fewer parts, less access, less support, same result more slowly. Keep the promise, shrink the package.

when.says: an upsell with a delivery cost you can shrink

steps: List the parts of the upsell
Remove the ones that cost you most and the customer least
Price it between the attraction offer and the upsell
Keep the string to continuity
Compare its take rate with the payment plan's

plays.label: Deposit and decide
plays.what: A small payment to hold the price or the spot, decided later. Cash today, and a reason to come back.

when.says: a cap per run, so holding a spot means something

steps: Set the deposit (5 to 10% of the upsell)
Say what it holds: the price, the spot, the bonus
Set the decide-by date
Follow up the day before
Count deposits, conversions and refunds

plays.label: Bonus for committing
plays.what: A gift, worth a lot to them and little to you, for joining the ongoing plan today.

when.says: a continuity join rate under 70%, so the first no is the problem

steps: Pick a bonus that costs you under one month's gross profit
Make it available only at joining
Say it in the pitch
Count join rates with and without it
Rotate it every quarter

plays.label: Discount for a longer term
plays.what: Pay for a year, get it cheaper. Cash forward, churn removed.

when.says: members staying six months or more on average, so a year is believable

steps: Price the year at ten months or so
Offer it at joining and at month three
Show the monthly price beside it
Count yearly takers
Put the cash in the 30-day figure on level C13

plays.label: Waived fee
plays.what: The setup or first month is free if they join now. The fee exists so waiving it means something.

when.says: a continuity offer that makes a gross profit each month

steps: Add a real setup fee to the price list
Waive it for joining on the day
Bill the first month at joining
Count join rates before and after
Keep the fee on the list

plays.label: Bonuses over time
plays.what: Something new arrives in month two, three and six. Reasons to stay, not just reasons to join.

when.says: monthly churn of 5% or more, so staying is the problem

steps: List one thing to add in months two, three and six
Announce the schedule at joining
Deliver on the day, and say so
Watch churn by cohort
Move the best bonus earlier if month two leaks

plays.label: The default
plays.what: The ongoing plan is the normal thing to buy; the one-off is the exception you have to ask for.

when.says: a continuity price

steps: Put the ongoing plan first on every price list
Price the one-off higher per month than the plan
Train the script to assume the plan
Count how many ask for the one-off
Remove the one-off if under one in ten ask
